title: Redirect Loop (ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS)
description: Stop infinite redirect loops between http/https, www/non-www, or misconfigured plugins and server rules.

steps.title: Trace the Redirect Chain
steps.instructions: Use curl -I or browser DevTools Network tab to see each redirect hop. Note if it bounces between http/https or www/non-www variants.

steps.title: Align WordPress URLs with Actual Access URL
steps.instructions: Settings → General siteurl and home must match how users reach the site (https, www). Update wp-config constants if the database values are wrong.

steps.title: Check SSL and Really Simple SSL Settings
steps.instructions: SSL plugins can force https while the server also redirects — causing a loop. Disable one layer or set FORCE_SSL_ADMIN only in wp-config.

steps.title: Review Server and CDN Redirect Rules
steps.instructions: Compare Apache/nginx redirects, Cloudflare SSL mode, and host 'force HTTPS' toggles. Only one layer should canonicalize protocol and hostname.

steps.title: Fix COOKIE_DOMAIN and Proxy Headers
steps.instructions: Behind load balancers, ensure HTTPS is detected via $_SERVER['HTTPS'] or HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO. Wrong detection causes login and front-end redirect loops.

steps.title: Audit Redirection Plugin Rules
steps.instructions: Export and review redirect rules for regex loops (A→B→A). Disable the Redirection plugin temporarily to test if loops stop.

steps.title: Verify Clean Single Redirect
steps.instructions: Confirm one 301 from alternate URLs to canonical. Test homepage, wp-login.php, and wp-admin with curl -IL from external network.
